source.name: Elon Musk Archive
source.note: 数据来自 silicon-valley.tech 公开语料，遵循其 CC 条款：研究与引用须注明原始出处。

claim: Tesla's secret master plan: a sports car, then a cheaper sedan, then an affordable mass-market car.
Le plan secret de Tesla : une voiture de sport, puis une berline moins chère, puis une voiture abordable pour le grand public.
promises.quote: Build sports car. Use that money to build an affordable car. Use that money to build an even more affordable car.
promises.src: Tesla blog post “The Secret Tesla Motors Master Plan (just between you and me)”
outcome: Done in order: Roadster (2008), Model S (2012), Model 3 (2017).
Réalisé dans l'ordre : Roadster (2008), Model S (2012), Model 3 (2017).

claim: SpaceX will land and reuse orbital rocket boosters.
SpaceX fera atterrir et réutilisera les premiers étages de ses fusées orbitales.
promises.src: Repeated from 2011 onward (National Press Club, AIAA, Falcon Heavy press conference)
outcome: First landing December 21, 2015; first reflight March 30, 2017. Reuse is now routine.
Premier atterrissage le 21 décembre 2015, premier revol le 30 mars 2017. La réutilisation est désormais la norme.

claim: Falcon Heavy will make its first flight in 2013.
La Falcon Heavy fera son premier vol en 2013.
outcome: First flight on February 6, 2018, about five years late. It worked, side boosters landed together.
Premier vol le 6 février 2018, environ cinq ans plus tard que prévu. Le vol a réussi et les deux propulseurs latéraux ont atterri ensemble.

claim: A Tesla will drive itself from Los Angeles to New York, with no touch of the controls, by the end of 2017.
Une Tesla traversera les États-Unis, de Los Angeles à New York, sans que personne ne touche les commandes, d'ici fin 2017.
promises.src: Tesla press call announcing Hardware 2, October 2016
outcome: Never done as announced. Tesla has not published such a fully hands-off coast-to-coast drive.
Jamais réalisé comme annoncé. Tesla n'a publié aucune traversée entièrement autonome de ce type.

claim: Model 3 production will reach 5,000 cars a week by December 2017.
La Model 3 sera produite à 5 000 exemplaires par semaine dès décembre 2017.
outcome: Reached in the last week of June 2018, about six months late, after what Musk called “production hell”.
Atteint la dernière semaine de juin 2018, environ six mois plus tard, après ce que Musk a appelé « l'enfer de la production ».

claim: First cargo ships to Mars in 2022, first crew in 2024.
Premiers vaisseaux cargo vers Mars en 2022, premier équipage en 2024.
outcome: No Starship has flown to Mars yet. Starship flew its first full test in April 2023.
Aucun Starship n'est encore parti vers Mars. Starship a fait son premier vol d'essai complet en avril 2023.

claim: Tesla Semi production will start in 2019.
La production du Tesla Semi commencera en 2019.
outcome: First deliveries in December 2022 (PepsiCo), in small numbers; high-volume production was still being prepared in 2026.
Premières livraisons en décembre 2022 (PepsiCo), en petit nombre ; la production en volume était encore en préparation en 2026.

claim: Tesla could have a million robotaxis on the road by the end of 2020.
Tesla pourrait avoir un million de robotaxis en circulation fin 2020.
promises.quote: This is why it's possible for Tesla to have a million robotaxis by end of 2020 if we upgrade existing HW2 fleet of ~500k & make at least ~500k FSD cars
outcome: No robotaxis in 2020. Tesla launched a small paid robotaxi pilot in Austin in June 2025, with safety monitors on board.
Aucun robotaxi en 2020. Tesla a lancé un petit service payant de robotaxis à Austin en juin 2025, avec un employé de sécurité à bord.

claim: Model 3 volume production at Gigafactory Shanghai by the end of 2019.
Production en volume de la Model 3 à la Gigafactory de Shanghai fin 2019.
promises.quote: By the end of this year, we will -- we expect to be producing Model 3's in volume out of Gigafactory Shanghai
outcome: The factory was built in under a year; first customer deliveries of Shanghai-made Model 3s on December 30, 2019.
L'usine a été construite en moins d'un an ; premières livraisons de Model 3 fabriquées à Shanghai le 30 décembre 2019.

claim: The Model S Plaid will go into production around October–November 2020.
La Model S Plaid entrera en production vers octobre-novembre 2020.
promises.quote: We expect these track times to be beaten by the actual production 7 seat Model S Plaid variant that goes into production around Oct/Nov next year.
outcome: First deliveries in June 2021, about seven months late, and in a 5-seat version.
Premières livraisons en juin 2021, environ sept mois plus tard, et en version 5 places.

claim: Full Self-Driving will be “feature complete” by the end of 2019: the car drives from home to work, most likely without interventions.
La conduite autonome (FSD) sera « complète en fonctionnalités » fin 2019 : la voiture ira de la maison au travail, très probablement sans intervention.
promises.quote: Feature-complete, I mean, it's -- the car is able to drive from one's house to work, most likely without interventions. So it will still be supervised...
outcome: FSD Beta reached a first group of owners in October 2020. As of 2026 it is still sold as “FSD (Supervised)”: the driver must stay attentive.
La version bêta est arrivée chez un premier groupe de clients en octobre 2020. En 2026, elle est toujours vendue comme « FSD (Supervised) » : le conducteur doit rester attentif.

claim: Cybertruck production will start in late 2021.
La production du Cybertruck commencera fin 2021.
outcome: First deliveries on November 30, 2023, two years late.
Premières livraisons le 30 novembre 2023, deux ans plus tard que prévu.

claim: Neuralink may implant a human as soon as 2020.
Neuralink pourrait implanter un premier humain dès 2020.
promises.quote: Neuralink may have this in a human as soon as this year.
outcome: Repeated in 2021 (“later this year”). First human implant in January 2024 (Noland Arbaugh).
Répété en 2021 (« plus tard cette année »). Premier implant humain en janvier 2024 (Noland Arbaugh).

claim: Close to zero new COVID-19 cases in the US by the end of April 2020.
Presque plus aucun nouveau cas de Covid-19 aux États-Unis fin avril 2020.
promises.quote: Based on current trends, probably close to zero new cases in US too by end of April
outcome: The US was still recording around 25,000 to 30,000 new cases a day at the end of April 2020.
Les États-Unis comptaient encore environ 25 000 à 30 000 nouveaux cas par jour fin avril 2020.

claim: SpaceX aims for 48 launches in 2021.
SpaceX vise 48 lancements en 2021.
promises.quote: We will need to make a lot of improvements to have a chance of completing 48 launches next year!
outcome: SpaceX flew 31 Falcon 9 missions in 2021. The cadence then exploded: 61 in 2022, 96 in 2023.
SpaceX a effectué 31 lancements de Falcon 9 en 2021. La cadence a ensuite explosé : 61 en 2022, 96 en 2023.

claim: Two main goals for 2022: Starship to orbit and a wide release of FSD.
Deux objectifs principaux pour 2022 : Starship en orbite et FSD disponible pour tous.
promises.quote: 2 main goals this year: - Starship to orbit - FSD wide release
outcome: Starship's first full flight came in April 2023 and ended in an explosion; it reached space on a near-orbital path in March 2024. FSD Beta opened to all North American buyers in November 2022.

Le premier vol complet de Starship a eu lieu en avril 2023 et s'est terminé par une explosion ; il a atteint l'espace sur une trajectoire quasi orbitale en mars 2024. La bêta FSD a été ouverte à tous les acheteurs nord-américains en novembre 2022.

claim: AI will probably be smarter than any single human in 2025, and smarter than all humans combined by 2029.
L'IA sera probablement plus intelligente que n'importe quel humain en 2025, et que tous les humains réunis d'ici 2029.
promises.quote: AI will probably be smarter than any single human next year. By 2029, AI is probably smarter than all humans combined.
outcome: No agreed test exists. In January 2026 he moved the first milestone to “the end of this year… no later than next year”.
Il n'existe aucun test reconnu. En janvier 2026, il a repoussé la première étape à « la fin de cette année… au plus tard l'an prochain ».

claim: DOGE can cut at least $2 trillion from the US federal budget.
DOGE peut réduire le budget fédéral américain d'au moins 2 000 milliards de dollars.
promises.src: Trump rally at Madison Square Garden, October 2024
outcome: Musk lowered the target to $1 trillion, then $150 billion. DOGE's own website claimed savings of under $200 billion by mid-2025; independent reviews found many of those claims overstated.

Musk a abaissé l'objectif à 1 000 milliards, puis à 150 milliards. Le site de DOGE revendiquait moins de 200 milliards d'économies mi-2025 ; des vérifications indépendantes ont jugé beaucoup de ces chiffres surévalués.

claim: Many Starships will go to Mars in the 2026 transfer window.
De nombreux Starship partiront pour Mars lors de la fenêtre de tir de 2026.
promises.quote: Many Starships will go to Mars in 2 years, when the transit window opens again.
outcome: The 2026 window is open now. Not resolved yet.
La fenêtre de 2026 est ouverte en ce moment. Pas encore tranché.

claim: Starship will leave for Mars at the end of 2026, carrying Optimus robots; human landings as soon as 2029, more likely 2031.
Starship partira pour Mars fin 2026 avec des robots Optimus ; premiers humains sur Mars dès 2029, plus probablement en 2031.
promises.quote: Starship departs for Mars at the end of next year, carrying Optimus. If those landings go well, then human landings may start as soon as 2029, although 2031 is more likely.
outcome: The Mars launch window opens in late 2026. Not resolved yet.
La fenêtre de tir vers Mars s'ouvre fin 2026. Pas encore tranché.

claim: Millions of Teslas operating fully autonomously in the second half of 2026.
Des millions de Tesla rouleront de façon entièrement autonome au second semestre 2026.
promises.quote: I predict that there'll be millions of Teslas operating fully autonomously in the second half of next year.
outcome: Deadline is the end of 2026. Not resolved yet.
Échéance fin 2026. Pas encore tranché.

claim: AI smarter than any human by the end of 2026, no later than 2027.
Une IA plus intelligente que n'importe quel humain d'ici fin 2026, au plus tard en 2027.
promises.quote: I think we might have AI that is smarter than any human by the end of this year. And I would say no later than next year.
outcome: Not resolved yet.
Pas encore tranché.

why: 2008, the year Tesla and SpaceX both nearly went under. No stage, no slides: he stands in a Hollywood living room and pitches a $109,000 electric car to a small crowd, with nothing but conviction.

2008, l'année où Tesla et SpaceX ont toutes deux failli couler. Pas de scène, pas de slides : debout dans un salon d'Hollywood, il présente une voiture électrique à 109 000 $ à une petite assemblée, avec pour seule arme sa conviction.

Three Falcon 1 launches had failed. He had money for one more. On 28 September 2008 the fourth one reached orbit, the first privately built liquid-fuel rocket to do it. This link skips the 40-minute webcast and starts on his statement that night.

Trois lancements de Falcon 1 avaient échoué. Il lui restait de quoi en tenter un dernier. Le 28 septembre 2008, le quatrième atteint l'orbite : la première fusée à carburant liquide construite par une entreprise privée. Ce lien saute les 40 minutes de retransmission et démarre directement sur sa déclaration du soir.

The interview where he chokes up when he hears that Neil Armstrong and Gene Cernan, his heroes, testified against commercial spaceflight. And the line: “I don't ever give up. I'd have to be dead or completely incapacitated.”

L'interview où il a la gorge nouée en apprenant que Neil Armstrong et Gene Cernan, ses héros, ont témoigné contre les vols spatiaux commerciaux. Et la phrase : « Je n'abandonne jamais. Il faudrait que je sois mort ou complètement hors d'état. »

A calm, honest conversation about 2008, the worst year of his life, and the origin of his favourite method: reasoning from first principles instead of by analogy. The famous battery-cost example comes from here.

Une conversation calme et sincère sur 2008, la pire année de sa vie, et l'origine de sa méthode fétiche : raisonner à partir des principes premiers plutôt que par analogie. Le fameux exemple du coût des batteries vient d'ici.
2003, age 32, at Stanford. SpaceX is a year old and has not flown anything; everyone thinks it will fail. He explains, step by step and without bravado, why he is doing it anyway.
2003, 32 ans, à Stanford. SpaceX a un an et n'a encore rien lancé ; tout le monde pense que ça va échouer. Il explique, pas à pas et sans fanfaronner, pourquoi il le fait quand même.
1999, age 27, taking delivery of the McLaren F1 he bought after selling Zip2. A few years earlier he was sleeping in the office and showering at the YMCA. The starting line.
1999, 27 ans, il reçoit la McLaren F1 achetée après la vente de Zip2. Quelques années plus tôt, il dormait au bureau et se douchait au YMCA. La ligne de départ.
Caltech commencement, 2012: how he chose to work on the internet, sustainable energy and space, the things that would most affect the future of humanity, and why you should pick problems that matter.

Discours de remise des diplômes à Caltech, 2012 : comment il a choisi Internet, l'énergie durable et l'espace, les sujets qui allaient le plus peser sur l'avenir de l'humanité, et pourquoi il faut s'attaquer à des problèmes qui comptent.

USC, 2014. His five pieces of advice in under eight minutes: work super hard (80 to 100 hours a week), attract great people, focus on the signal over the noise, don't just follow the trend, and take risks while you can.

USC, 2014. Ses cinq conseils en moins de huit minutes : travailler extrêmement dur (80 à 100 heures par semaine), attirer des gens brillants, se concentrer sur le signal plutôt que le bruit, ne pas suivre la tendance, et prendre des risques tant qu'on le peut.
TED 2017. Tunnels, Tesla, Mars, and the closing answer about why he does it: you want to wake up in the morning and think the future is going to be great. Being a multi-planet species is about that.

TED 2017. Tunnels, Tesla, Mars, et la réponse finale sur pourquoi il fait tout ça : on veut se réveiller le matin en pensant que l'avenir sera formidable. Devenir une espèce multiplanétaire, c'est pour ça.
Hours after the first Falcon Heavy launch in February 2018, with his Roadster heading into space and two boosters landing side by side. Visibly elated: “Crazy things can come true.”

Quelques heures après le premier lancement du Falcon Heavy en février 2018, sa Roadster en route vers l'espace et deux boosters posés côte à côte. Visiblement aux anges : « Des choses folles peuvent devenir réalité. »

title: Artificial intelligence
Intelligence artificielle
intro: From 2014 he called AI humanity's biggest existential risk and pushed for regulation, co-founded OpenAI in 2015, then launched xAI in 2023 to build it himself.
Dès 2014, il qualifie l'IA de plus grand risque existentiel pour l'humanité et réclame une régulation ; il cofonde OpenAI en 2015, puis lance xAI en 2023 pour la construire lui-même.

2014.t: Hope we're not just the biological boot loader for digital superintelligence. Unfortunately, that is increasingly probable
Worth reading Superintelligence by Bostrom. We need to be super careful with AI. Potentially more dangerous than nukes.

2015.t: If you're against a military AI arms race, please sign this open letter:
World's top artificial intelligence developers sign open letter calling for AI safety research:

2016.t: Would like to thank @nvidia and Jensen for donating the first DGX-1 AI supercomputer to @OpenAI in support of democratizing AI technology
Only a matter of time before advanced AI is used to do this. Internet is particularly susceptible to a gradient descent algo.

2017.t: Nobody likes being regulated, but everything (cars, planes, food, drugs, etc) that's a danger to the public is regulated. AI should be too.
If you're not concerned about AI safety, you should be. Vastly more risk than North Korea.

2018.t: Nothing will affect the future of humanity more than digital super-intelligence. Watch Chris Paine's new AI movie for free until Sunday night at

Yes, I made this comment some years ago, but it feels like we are the biological bootloader for AI. Effectively, we are building it and then we’re building progressively greater intelligence and the percentage of intelligence that is not human is increasing and eventually we will represent a very small percentage of intelligence.
But the AI isn’t formed strangely by the human limbic system. It is in large part our ID writ large.

2019.t: If advanced AI (beyond basic bots) hasn't been applied to manipulate social media, it won't be long before it is

2020.t: What if there was an AI programmed to want to pick as many strawberries as possible, and so it cultivated nothing but strawberries on all of Earth's land? Then it would be Strawberry Fields Forever!
Tesla is developing a NN training computer called Dojo to process truly vast amounts of video data. It's a beast! Please consider joining our AI or computer/chip teams if this sounds interesting.

Yeah. Great. Wonderful. It's great. But babies are awesome. Yeah, it's great. Yeah. Also, I've spent a lot of time on AI and neural nets and so you can sort of see the brain develop, which is ... An AI neural net is trying to simulate what a brain does, basically. You can sort of see it learning very quickly. You know, it's just wow.

2021.t: A major part of real-world AI has to be solved to make unsupervised, generalized full self-driving work, as the entire road system is designed for biological neural nets with optical imagers
So much of AI is about compressing reality to a small vector space, like a video game in reverse

2022.t: Even some of the best AI software engineers in the world don't realize how advanced Tesla AI has become

Tesla Full Self-Driving Beta is now available to anyone in North America who requests it from the car screen, assuming you have bought this option. 

Congrats to Tesla Autopilot/AI team on achieving a major milestone!

2023.t: Some wild decisions will come up in the future about AI programs

Old joke about agnostic technologists building artificial super intelligence to find out if there's a God.

They finally finish & ask the question.

AI replies: "There is now, mfs!!"

But yeah, there's really some amazing AI generator clothing. It's really cool. And I really love that one with the Pope and that went viral. A lot of people thought that the Pope actually had that outfit, which is not totally out of the question because there's a lot of amazing fashion in Italy. So it's possible that some fashion house made a really epic coat for the Pope. But that was obviously AI generated. We're headed into a weird world here. Speaker 6 : We are, video games.

I don’t personally use it, but for teenagers and people in their 20s, they seem almost religiously addicted to TikTok. Some people will watch TikTok for two hours a day. I stopped using TikTok when I felt the AI probing my mind and it made me uncomfortable, so I stopped using it. And in terms of antisemitic content, TikTok is rife with that. It has the most viral antisemitic content by far.

2024.t: Video of the inside of Cortex today, the giant new AI training supercluster being built at Tesla HQ in Austin to solve real-world AI
We should eliminate electronic voting machines. The risk of being hacked by humans or AI, while small, is still too high.

Yeah. I think it’s important that whatever AI wins, it’s a maximum truth seeking AI that is not forced to lie for political correctness, or, well, for any reason, really, political, anything. I am concerned about AI succeeding that is programmed to lie, even in small ways.

In the short term. But even for AI, you really have a growing demand for electricity, for electric vehicles, and a growing demand for electricity to run the computers for AI. And so this is obviously, can lead to electricity shortage.

2025.t:
Grok 3 release with live demo on Monday night at 8pm PT. 

Smartest AI on Earth.
As I mentioned several years ago, it increasingly appears that humanity is a biological bootloader for digital superintelligence

Well, I mean, I think actually long term, the AI is going to be in charge, to be totally frank, not humans. If artificial intelligence vastly exceeds the sum of human intelligence, it is difficult to imagine that any humans will actually be in charge. So we just need to make sure that AI is friendly.
AI could certainly emulate a scarred human being quite well. Yeah. I mean, the AI video generation that I’m seeing at xAI and from others is pretty impressive.

2026.t: Yeah, so we do intend with our SpaceX AI satellites, to allow people to put whatever GPU or TPU they want. So NVIDIA GPUs can be put on it, Google TPUs can be put on it, Amazon Trainiums or any other chips that people want to put on can be put on. We will also offer our chips in the future, and I think we also want to offer our software, our AI software as well in the future. But it will be such that you can run anyone’s AI hardware or software on the SpaceX AI satellites.

It used to be. At this point, I don’t know. I wouldn’t say there’s anything particularly keeping me up at night right now, except that if you say, why do I wake up in nightmares? AI. Yeah. Actually I’ve had a lot of AI nightmares. I had AI nightmares many days in a row. What am I supposed to do about it?

title: Mars & becoming multiplanetary
Mars et l'humanité multiplanétaire
intro: The founding idea of SpaceX in 2002: make life multiplanetary as a backup for civilisation. The target date for the first trip has moved many times.
L'idée fondatrice de SpaceX en 2002 : rendre la vie multiplanétaire pour sauvegarder la civilisation. La date du premier voyage a souvent été repoussée.

2013.t: No near term plans to IPO @SpaceX. Only possible in very long term when Mars Colonial Transporter is flying regularly.

2015.t: The rumor that I'm building a spaceship to get back to my home planet Mars is totally untrue
Btw, not saying we *should* nuke Mars -- just layin' out a few options …

2016.t: To activate the Model X holiday performance, just type holidays or ModelXmas after pressing the logo. Also, Mars.

2017.t: It is high time that humanity went beyond Earth. Should have a moon base by now and sent astronauts to Mars. The future needs to inspire.

Last pic of Starman in Roadster on its journey to Mars orbit and then the Asteroid Belt

2019.t: Tesla Cybertruck (pressurized edition) will be official truck of Mars

Megatons per year to orbit are needed for life to become multiplanetary

2023.t:
For the first time, there is a rocket that can make all life multiplanetary.

Starship will make life multiplanetary, preserving life as know from extinction events on Earth, so long as it is not smothered by bureaucracy.

Trump supports a government efficiency commission to…

Yeah. So aliens, I mean, I don’t know. Look, I think the smart move is just this is the first time in the history of earth that it’s been possible for life to extend beyond earth. That window is open. Now it may be open for a long time or it may be open for a short time and it may be open now and then never open again. So I think the smart move here is to make life multiplanetary while it’s possible to do so. We don’t want to be one of those lame one planet civilizations that just dies out.

I think we’re all affected by the people we grew up with. My aspiration is to do whatever it takes to extend consciousness into the future. That’s my goal, to make life multi-planetary as part of extending consciousness into the future.

Starship will hopefully depart for Mars at the end of next year with Optimus explorer robots!

Well, Optimus is going to play a big role. Optimus and, I think, Tesla vehicles will play a big role on the moon and Mars. So for a moon base and a Mars city, Tesla vehicles and Optimus robots are natural fit for building and operating a moon base than a Mars city.

I mean, I might go to Mars, but that'll be part of America. Yeah.

title: Birth rate & population
Natalité et population
intro: Once a footnote, falling birth rates became one of his most repeated themes from around 2017, framed as a bigger threat than climate change.
Sujet secondaire au départ, la baisse de la natalité devient à partir de 2017 environ l'un de ses thèmes les plus répétés, présentée comme une menace plus grave que le climat.

2021.t:
Population collapse is potentially the greatest risk to the future of civilization
wsj.com/articles/u-s-p…

2022.t: Population collapse due to low birth rates is a much bigger risk to civilization than global warming
USA birth rate has been below min sustainable levels for ~50 years

2023.t: Very interesting. Hungary is trying hard to address their birth rate problem.
Great meeting with the President of Hungary about the population collapse crisis!

2024.t: Birth rates continue to plummet. Population collapse is coming.
2/3 of Korea will disappear every generation. Population collapse.

It doesn’t produce kids. Well, what matters… I mean, Durant makes this very clear because he’s looked at one civilization after another and they all went through the same cycle. When the civilization was under stress, the birth rate was high. But as soon as there were no external enemies or they had an extended period of prosperity, the birth rate inevitably dropped. Every time. I don’t believe there’s a single exception.

2025.t:
Many countries are disappearing. 

Immigration cannot solve billions in population collapse. It simply isn't physically possible. 

More importantly, we should not lose entire, distinct cultures!

This is how great civilizations throughout history have ended.

People assume it was due to conquest, but it was actually often simply too much prosperity leading to low birth rate and population collapse, which ultimately enabled them to be conquered.

Yeah.

title: Free speech
Liberté d'expression
intro: The stated reason for buying Twitter in 2022. The theme grows sharply from that year, along with fights with governments and advertisers.
La raison avancée pour racheter Twitter en 2022. Le thème explose à partir de cette année-là, avec des conflits contre des gouvernements et des annonceurs.

2022.t: I hope that even my worst critics remain on Twitter, because that is what free speech means
The extreme antibody reaction from those who fear free speech says it all

2023.t: To be super clear, I'm pro free speech, but against anti-Semitism of any kind
Best way to fight misinformation is to respond with accurate information, not censorship

Yeah. So Starlink, there’s several thousand satellites in low earth orbit and they’re moving around 25 times the speed of sound in these—they’re zipping around the earth basically. And they’re at an altitude of about 550 kilometers, which is called generally low earth orbit.
Because they’re at low earth orbit, the latency is low, like the distance, because the distance is not that far compared to a geostationary satellite, 36,000 kilometers. So you’ve got thousands of satellites providing low latency high speed Internet throughout the world.
And they are interconnected as well. So there’s laser links between the satellites. So it forms sort of a laser mesh so that the—if, let’s say, let’s say if cables are damaged or cut like fiber cables, the satellites can communicate between each other and provide connectivity even if the cables are cut.
So for example, when the Red Sea cables were cut, I think a few months ago, the Starlink satellite network continued to function without a hitch. So it’s particularly helpful for disaster areas. So if an area has been hit with some kind of natural disaster, floods or fires or earthquakes, that tends to damage the ground infrastructure. But the Starlink satellites still work.
So and generally whenever there’s some sort of natural disaster somewhere, we always provide people with free Starlink Internet connectivity. You know, we don’t want to charge, we don’t want to take advantage of a tragic situation. So if there’s natural disasters, we’re like, okay, it’s free during the natural disaster. You know, we don’t want to say like put a paywall up while somebody’s trying to get help. That would be wrong.
So, so that’s, it’s a very robust system. It’s complementary to ground systems because the satellite beams work best in sparsely populated areas. But because you’ve got it, you’ve got a satellite beam, it’s a pretty big beam. So you have, and you have a fixed number of users per beam.
So it tends to be very complementary to the ground based cellular systems because those are very good in cities because you’ve got these cell towers that are, you know, only a kilometer apart type of thing. But cell towers tend to be inefficient in the countryside.
So in rural areas is where you tend to have the worst Internet because it’s very expensive, difficult to lay to do all these, do all the fiber optic cables or to have high bandwidth cellular towers. So Starlink is very complementary to the existing telecom companies. It basically tends to serve the least served, which I think is good.
